To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the prompt hadro-production of charmonia and bottomonia is dominated by the fusion of (gg)8S and a gluon; (ii) the cross section is enhanced by a factor of about 10 compared with previous perturbatively-calculated values; (iii) the predicted cross sections are in excellent agreement with the experimental data, and (iv) the predicted cross section ratios are in good agreement with those measured in $pp$ collisions at LHC.

the prompt production of the $J/\psi$, $\psi'$ and the bottomonia states at the Tevatrons and RHICs are well described in the leading-order approximation of perturbative QGCD by the fusion of two gluons into the symmetric colour-octets states (gg)8S and (ggg)8S followed by a gluon emission.
the colour-octet mechanism is able to describe the prompt hadro-production of the $J/\psi$, $\psi'$ and $\Upsilon(nS)$ states at the Tevatton, RHIC and the LHC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prompt hadro-production of charmonium and bottomonium in leading order perturbative Q CD.
the production of $J/\Psi$ and $\Upsi$ at high energy hadron colliders.
the prompt hadro-production of the $J/\psi,\psi'$ and the $Upsilon$ states caused by the gluon-gluon fusion of a symmetric $gg8$ colour-octet and an additional gluons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the colour-octet gluon-gluon fusion is the dominant production mechanism for the prompt production of charmonia at hadron colliders, and the colour-octect state (gg)8S is the dominant source for the production of bottomonia.

the colour-octet mechanism is the main source for the inelastic hadroproduction of the $J/\psi$, $\psi'$ and $\Upsilon (nS)$ states, and that the corresponding cross sections are consistent with the measured values.

the colour-octet model, in the context of the present study, can explain the data on the prompt hadro production of $J/\Psi$, $\psi'$ and $\Upsilon (nS)$, without the need for invoking non-perturbatively motivated contributions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we are able to reproduce the data with a single set of parameters, which are fixed by the inclusive cross sections for the $J/\psi$, $\Upsilon (nS)$ production and the $J/\phi$, $\Upsilon$ polarisation data.
the perturbative QGP scenario is consistent with the experimental measurements.
the prompt hadro-production of $c\bar c$ and $b\bar b$ pairs in the colour-octet channel, (gg) 8s + g $\to$ $c\bar{c},\ b\bar b$, provides a good phenomenological description of the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the colour-octet mechanism is not required to understand the prompt hadro-production of $J/\Psi$ and $\Upsi$.
the perturbative production of colour-octet states can be a significant source of $J/\Psi, \Upsilon$ mesons.
the perturbative Q CD predictions are in good agreement with the data for the prompt production of $J/\ψ$ and $ψ'$ at the Tevattron, RHIC and the LHC.
